thread:
maya: Heads up — eval runner showing nondeterministic EM scores on the new quantized-flan bring-up. Same model+prompts, 3 runs with seed=42 produce EM 78.1 / 79.9 / 78.3. Not a CI flake; I reproduced locally.
maya: Repro steps: checkout branch `quant-int8-onboard`, run `tools/eval_runner --suite squad_v2 --model ./artifacts/flanq-int8 --sampling --temp 0.7 --top_p 0.9 --seed 42 --runs 3`. Logs: https://redwood-repro/gists/3482
maya: Quick paste of the sampling config we're passing in eval runner:
```
{"sampling": true, "temperature": 0.7, "top_p": 0.9, "seed": 42, "samples_per_prompt": 1}
```
ravi: hmm. First thought: are we reseeding per-batch somewhere? I remember a previous bug where we call `np.random.seed(self.seed)` inside the loop instead of using a generator instance.
thomas: could also be deterministic differences from quant kernels. int8 kernels sometimes use nondet fused ops (atomic adds, parallel kernels). But the numbers you show (1–2 point swings) feel more like sampling RNG drifting.
alex: do you see diffs in logits across runs before sampling? run with `--dump-logits` for a few examples and compare hashes. If logits differ, it's RNG earlier in the pipeline or kernel nondet. If logits same and outputs different -> sampling layer wrong.
maya: good point. I ran with `--dump-logits` for a single prompt. Logit hashes were identical across runs. So sampling RNG looks suspect.
ravi: paste of the relevant eval-runner loop:
```
for prompt in prompts:
    if config.sampling:
        random.seed(config.seed)
        samples = sample_from_logits(logits, temperature=config.temperature, top_p=config.top_p)
    else:
        samples = greedy_decode(logits)
```
ravi: this is wrong — reseeding on every prompt yields correlated but not identical sequences depending on internal state of sample_from_logits (like if it uses additional RNG calls for top_p thresholding). Also if `sample_from_logits` uses torch's RNG while we seed python's `random`, mismatch.
thomas: yep. We need to centralize RNG. Our model vendor sampling code uses `torch.multinomial` which consumes torch RNG, so seeding python.Random is useless. We should create a `torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)` per run and pass it to torch.multinomial.
alex: additional nuance: when using CUDA the generator can be nondet across different CUDA versions/drivers. For determinism in tests we should use CPU sampling or float32 kernels for the deterministic CI gate.
maya: plan suggestion:
- create EvalRunner.rng = torch.Generator(device=device) seeded once per run
- pass generator into sampling ops (multinomial, any torch sampling)
- remove per-prompt reseed
- add a lightweight determinism test in CI that runs 3 repeats and asserts stable EM (or exact token-level equality when sampling disabled)
ravi: I'll open a PR for the rng change. Also add an env var EVAL_FORCE_CPU_SAMPLING to help CI isolate kernel nondet issues.
thomas: for int8 quant kernels: we should also add an instrumented mode that forces fp32 path to check whether nondet originates in quant kernels. Add `--force-fp32` toggle.
alex: for metrics: EM fluctuates a bit when sampling enabled — maybe use majority-vote across k runs in the eval dashboard to avoid noisy regressions. But for gating model rollouts we want strict determinism, so CI must fail if the single-run EM differs from baseline beyond tolerance.
ci-bot: rerun requested by maya for `quant-int8-onboard` on commit 7a2f1d3 — queued.
maya: thanks. Ravi — can you also add a unit test that simulates top_p sampling edge case? e.g. when cumulative prob plateaus near cutoff, different implementations may call RNG extra times.
ravi: yep. I'll add `tests/test_sampling_determinism.py` with two scenarios: top_p and temperature, on CPU with seeded generator. It will compare tokens across 5 runs.
thomas: note for PR review: include a short explanation in the changelog about why we switched to torch.Generator and the CPU/FP32 debugging knobs.
maya: timeline: ravi to open PR today, thomas to add FP32 toggle, alex to update dashboard proposal (majority-vote option and per-eval-run stability score). I’ll triage any CI failures once CI finishes reruns.
alex: +1. Also add a small note in onboarding doc about "sampling determinism" — common pitfalls: reseeding per-prompt, mixing RNG libraries, CUDA kernel nondet.
maya: cool. If CI passes with CPU sampling deterministic, we'll try enabling int8 path and rerun the determinism test to isolate the kernel source.
alex: sounds good. ping me if you need a quick kernel repro harness; I have a small runner for quant kernels.
